findings.title: No tests for the email length limit, email trimming or empty email
findings.detail: The it.each table covers name >100 and message >2000, but no test reaches .max(255, 'Email maksimal 255 karakter') at contact.schema.ts:26. Email trimming and the "empty email reports wajib diisi, not a format error" order (contact.schema.ts:23-24) are also untested. Add rows for a 262-char email and an empty email, plus a padded email to the trim test.

findings.title: Abuse surface: public unauthenticated write, no throttle or body cap
findings.detail: Anyone can call this POST with no rate limit, CAPTCHA or honeypot, and every valid call writes a row upstream. await req.json() parses the whole body before any size check; the schema limits only bound what gets forwarded. Fix: reject early on Content-Length (e.g. >16 KB) and read with a size cap; add per-IP rate limiting plus a honeypot or CAPTCHA.

findings.title: Info exposure: upstream error envelope sent verbatim to anonymous callers
findings.detail: NextResponse.json(res) passes upstream code/message (copied by src/libs/api/server.ts:20-25) to unauthenticated clients. Fix: on success === false return a fixed generic message/code and log the upstream detail server-side.

findings.title: `ContactMessage` interface breaks the feature `I`-prefix convention
findings.detail: Every sibling features/<feature>/types/index.ts (users: IUser, roles: IRole, permissions: IPermission, branches: IBranch, profile: IMyProfile) prefixes entity interfaces with `I`. This file exports plain `ContactMessage`; rename to `IContactMessage` to match the established pattern.

findings.title: `ContactMessagePayload` breaks the feature `T`-prefix convention for payload types
findings.detail: Siblings name payload/list type aliases with a `T` prefix (TCreateUserPayload, TUpdateRolePayload, TCreatePermissionPayload, TUpdateProfilePayload). Should be `TContactMessagePayload` to stay consistent with every other feature's types/index.ts.

findings.title: `ContactMessageFieldErrors` also lacks the sibling `T` prefix
findings.detail: Same convention source (all non-interface type aliases in feature types/index.ts files are T-prefixed); low impact since route-local plumbing, rename for consistency (TContactMessageFieldErrors).
